subject: Tiered uptime override & monthly credit schedule — Cloudhaven request
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@cloudhaven.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudhaven.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tiered uptime override + monthly credit schedule

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood’s cost controls for high-throughput inference. Before we move to legal, procurement needs a concrete proposal for an uptime exception on our sandbox-heavy workload and how that maps to monthly service credits.

Two specifics from procurement:
- We need a temporary uptime floor of 96.5% for the first three months of the pilot (reason: heavy nightly batch jobs spike capacity usage).
- They want an explicit monthly credit schedule if availability drops below our standard 99.5% baseline after the pilot transitions to production.

Can you share a clear table showing credit percentages per availability band and confirm whether maintenance windows (scheduled and rolling) would be carved out from the measurement? Procurement also flagged a desire for a short-term waiver vs permanent SLA change — so language that allows a provisional exception would help.

I attached our internal procurement checklist (referenced only). Happy to hop on a call if it helps.

Best,
Alex
Account Lead — Cloudhaven Inc.
Attachment: cloudhaven-procurement-checklist.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@cloudhaven.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tiered uptime override + monthly credit schedule

Alex —

Really appreciate the clarity. Short answer: we can support a provisional uplift/override for the pilot period and map a tiered monthly credit schedule for production.

Quick notes up front:
- We typically measure baseline availability against 99.5% monthly. Temporary pilot exceptions are possible (with defined duration and sunset).
- Maintenance windows that are scheduled with 72+ hours' notice and listed in the contract are carved out; emergency maintenance is handled case-by-case and may not be carved out.

I’m looping in Marissa (contracts) to propose the exact credit bands and the wording for a provisional exception vs permanent SLA amendment. Marissa — can you propose a 3-month pilot waiver construct + a credits worksheet?

If it’s helpful I can schedule a 30-min call with procurement and your legal next week.

Thanks,
Sean
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@cloudhaven.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Sep 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tiered uptime override + monthly credit schedule

Alex / Sean —

Thanks for the context. Attached is a proposed worksheet (monthly-credit-worksheet.xlsx) and a short redline summary (cloudhaven-sla-redlines-v1.pdf). Summary highlights below — happy to iterate: 

1) Provisional pilot waiver (3 months)- Purpose: allow Cloudhaven to run nightly batch-heavy pilot without immediate SLA breach exposure.- Term: 90 days from pilot start date; after 90 days availability will be measured against the standard baseline unless parties agree to extend.- Effect: For the pilot term, Redwood will record availability against a provisional floor of 96.5% (as requested) for monitoring and won't trigger formal credit payouts unless availability falls below 94.0% for a given month.

2) Production monthly credit schedule (post-pilot)- Baseline: 99.5% monthly availability.- Credit bands (monthly uptime):
  - >= 99.5%: 0% credit
  - 99.0% - 99.49%: 5% of monthly invoice as credit
  - 98.0% - 98.99%: 15% credit
  - 96.5% - 97.99%: 35% credit
  - < 96.5%: 60% credit (or escalated remediation under contract)

3) Maintenance carveouts- Scheduled maintenance: carved out if posted in the maintenance calendar and communicated 72 hours prior.- Rolling capacity adjustments (planned scaling events): if customer is notified in advance, these are carved out from uptime calculations.- Emergency/unscheduled maintenance: not carved out by default; will be evaluated in post-incident review.

4) Measurement and verification- Redwood provides per-route monthly availability reports and raw traces upon request (redwood-monitoring link included). Credits are triggered after verification and mutual agreement; disputes go to a single escalation review within 10 business days.

5) Operational guardrail- During the pilot we propose a cap of one credit payout per month (i.e., credits don't compound intra-month) and an overall remediation cap equal to 100% of one month’s invoice per calendar quarter for production tiers.

Next steps we suggest:
- Confirm the pilot start window and whether Cloudhaven wants the waiver to be retroactive to an earlier start date.
- Procurement/Legal: confirm the carveout language in the attached redlines.

Attachments: monthly-credit-worksheet.xlsx (credit table + example calculation), cloudhaven-sla-redlines-v1.pdf (draft redlines).

Marissa Cole
Senior Contracts Manager — Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: monthly-credit-worksheet.xlsx, cloudhaven-sla-redlines-v1.pdf
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@cloudhaven.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudhaven.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2025 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tiered uptime override + monthly credit schedule

Marissa / Sean —

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement asked for. A couple quick items from Procurement: 
- They like the provisional floor approach and the 90-day sunset.
- They asked that the worksheet include one worked example for a 30-day invoice at $50k/month showing 35% credit math (the attached worksheet looks like it has that, will confirm).
- They asked for DocuSign-ready contract language; can you flag which clauses in the PDF are intended to be the waiver language so legal can pull them into their redlines?

Assuming no big objections from legal, we’re ready to move to DocuSign and sign the pilot waiver. Can you provide a DocuSign link or the next steps to get signatures?

Also, Sean — please schedule the 30-min kickoff with our ops/procurement next Tue 10–10:30 PT if that works for you and Marissa.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex
Account Lead — Cloudhaven Inc.
